reasons: Only the header of 806 lines was reviewed.
The render tests draw this view for every golden case, which is some evidence it does not crash on real data.
I did not run these tests in this review.

terms.meaning: a score where five is worse, not better
the time passing from start to finish, including waiting, which is different from effort

sections.name: File setup, INVERTED
sections.title: Page header and inverted scores
sections.what: Explains that the page shows one process at a time, marks two scores where five is worse, and marks elapsed hours rather than effort. Brings in the types, components and formatters, and sets the list of inverted scores.
sections.why: The header says a footnote is where a reader is not looking, and a rollup that treats all nine scores as higher-is-better would rank the hardest processes as the best.
sections.watch_out: Any new score that runs the other way must be added to the inverted set, or it will read backwards.

sections.name: DIMENSION_ORDER
sections.title: The list of scorecard dimensions
sections.what: Lists the nine scorecard dimensions in the order the process page shows them. The scorecard table is built from this list, not from the data itself.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed order keeps the table stable, and the list is also checked by the compile-time guards below.
sections.watch_out: A dimension missing from this list will not appear on the page, and only the compile-time check will flag it.

sections.name: Assert
sections.title: Compile-time check helper
sections.what: Defines a small type used only to make the build fail when a condition is false. It has no effect when the app runs.
sections.why: The comments explain that the type checker catches removed dimensions but not added ones, so this check closes that gap.
sections.watch_out: Its result is only visible when the build runs, so a passing app does not prove the check passed.

sections.name: UnorderedDimensions
sections.title: Names of unlisted scorecard dimensions
sections.what: Works out which scorecard dimensions are missing from the display list. It is exported so the build does not flag it as unused. It is meant to be read when the check below fails.
sections.why: The comment says it exists so a failing check names the missing dimensions directly.
sections.watch_out: It only reports, and the failure itself comes from the check below.

sections.name: EveryDimensionIsOrdered
sections.title: Check that every dimension is listed
sections.what: Forces the build to fail unless the missing-dimension list is empty.
sections.why: The comments say this prevents a dimension that was added during regeneration from silently disappearing from the table.
sections.watch_out: If the scorecard schema gains a field, the build fails until this list is updated.

sections.name: PARAMETERS
sections.title: Value parameters and how each is shown
sections.what: Lists each value parameter with its plain meaning and the formatter used to display it. Parameters are shown as ranges, never as money.
sections.why: The comment says it is written so that a figure from a cited source does not look like a guess, and two of the seven are guesses in the golden set.
sections.watch_out: Each entry must match a field name in the data exactly, or that parameter will show as missing.

sections.name: BandedParameter, UnrenderedParameters
sections.title: Banded parameters that are not shown
sections.what: Works out which range-type value parameters are not in the display list. The three list fields are excluded by name so that a new list field is not hidden by accident.
sections.why: The comments say excluding by name is used so that a new range field breaks the check, while a new list field does not.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new list field does not trigger the check. The field is only shown if it is rendered in its own section.

sections.name: EveryParameterIsRendered
sections.title: Check that every parameter is shown
sections.what: Forces the build to fail unless the list of unshown parameters is empty.
sections.why: Same reason as the dimension check: it stops a new parameter disappearing from the page without warning.
sections.watch_out: Adding a parameter to the data without listing it here breaks the build rather than the page.

sections.name: Process (part 1)
sections.title: Process page header and case picker
sections.what: Shows the page for one process. If no record exists for the chosen process, it shows a message explaining that nothing is rendered rather than an empty page. Otherwise it shows a row of buttons to choose any process, then the process name and its taxonomy path.
sections.why: The comment says the missing-record branch once lacked the run stamp, so it now includes it to keep the run details visible on every view.
sections.watch_out: The page reads the process record and its prerequisite links at the start, so a missing record must be handled before anything else reads it.

sections.name: Process (part 2)
sections.title: Identity of the process
sections.what: Shows the process's stable id, its name, whether it is a leaf step, its work unit, its annual volume as a range with evidence, and its purpose, trigger, output and framing evidence. A warning appears if the record notes an evidence gap.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The section is the first thing a reader needs to check that they are looking at the right process.
sections.watch_out: The annual volume is a range, not a single number, so do not quote it as one.

sections.name: Process (part 3)
sections.title: Current state steps
sections.what: Lists the process steps in order with their type, role, systems, elapsed time, effort share and evidence. A total row sums the effort shares.
sections.why: The section note explains that elapsed time and effort share are different measures, so a step can look large on one and small on the other.
sections.watch_out: Elapsed time is not effort. Reading a long elapsed step as a big effort step is the easiest mistake here.

sections.name: Process (part 4)
sections.title: Pain points and workflow debt
sections.what: Shows the recorded pain points as a list with severity and the steps they touch. Below it, a table lists workflow debt sorted from most to least severe.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Sorting by severity puts the worst problems first.
sections.watch_out: Severity is the record's own score, so it reflects the source judgement, not a measured value.

sections.name: Process (part 5)
sections.title: Scorecard and nature of work
sections.what: Shows the nine scorecard dimensions with their score, whether a high score is good or bad, the rationale and evidence. Two dimensions are marked as inverted, meaning 5 is worse. Below, four positional axes are shown from 0 to 100.
sections.why: The section note says the inverted dimensions are marked in the table itself so a reader cannot miss them.
sections.watch_out: The axes are positions, not scores, so there is no good end to any of them.

sections.name: Process (part 6)
sections.title: Future state, agents and future steps
sections.what: Shows the future purpose and posture, the agents designed for the process with their tools and data contracts, and the ordered future steps with who performs each one.
sections.why: The section note says a future state without an exception model is only a demonstration, which is why this section sits beside the exception model.
sections.watch_out: Missing tools or contracts show as none recorded, which can look the same as a real empty list.

sections.name: Process (part 7)
sections.title: Exception model and declared assumptions
sections.what: Shows escalation triggers, the human response time, and the fallback behaviour. It then lists each declared assumption with its resolution, whether it answers an objection, its evidence, and any warning about an invalid record or a cost note.
sections.why: The section note explains the three kinds of resolution and says that a declared prerequisite is grounded but still conditional.
sections.watch_out: An invalid record is shown with a warning and read as unsupported, so the page does not treat it as proven.

sections.name: Process (part 8)
sections.title: Feasibility limits and data readiness
sections.what: Shows the binding autonomy ceiling, the list of legal and policy constraints with their ceilings and affected steps, and the data the process needs, has, governs and lacks.
sections.why: The section note says this section shows what the design is not allowed to do and which ceiling applies.
sections.watch_out: The binding ceiling is recalculated from the constraints at build time, so it is the strictest one and not a free value.

sections.name: Process (part 9)
sections.title: Implications, the operating model
sections.what: Shows the evidence for the implications block and a list of operating model changes, each with its evidence. If the list is empty it says none recorded.
sections.why: The section note says the block is shown because its confidence score is shown, and a score for a block that is not visible would mislead.
sections.watch_out: An empty list reads as nothing changes, which may simply mean nothing was recorded.

sections.name: Process (part 10)
sections.title: Workforce direction and skills
sections.what: Shows, for each role, the direction of headcount change and the skills it gains or loses, with evidence. It never shows a headcount figure.
sections.why: The table caption explains that released effort is calculated elsewhere, so a headcount here would state a total the engine did not compute.
sections.watch_out: Only directions are shown, so a reader must not read them as numbers.

sections.name: Process (part 11)
sections.title: Value parameters, prerequisites and shared enablers
sections.what: Shows a basis banner for the parameters, then a table of each parameter with its low, base and high range. It lists shared enablers and the prerequisites that must land first. If there are no prerequisites, the process is marked as eligible for wave one.
sections.why: The section note says the basis is the key point, because a set derived from cited figures and one stated as a hypothesis look the same otherwise.
sections.watch_out: Parameters are estimated inputs, never currency amounts. Do not quote them as money.

sections.name: Process (part 12)
sections.title: Confidence per block and challenges from the critic
sections.what: Shows a warning explaining what the confidence numbers mean and do not mean. Then it lists each confidence block with its figure. A second table lists challenges from the critic, with the struck evidence and whether each challenge was upheld.
sections.why: The warning exists because the same number meant something different under the previous schema, and it does not measure whether sources agree.
sections.watch_out: A confidence number is never a bare score. Read it with its citations and gaps, and remember it does not measure agreement.

sections.name: standingFor
sections.title: Choosing the standing of a resolution
sections.what: Decides which label a claim gets. A declared prerequisite with evidence is its own category. A declared prerequisite with no evidence falls back to unsupported.
sections.why: The comment explains that the chip and the panel must not say contradictory things about one claim, so the invalid case is read the safer way.
sections.watch_out: The schema and the evaluation gate reject the empty-evidence combination, so reaching this path means a bad record got past both.

sections.name: invalidResolutionNote
sections.title: Warning for an invalid resolution
sections.what: Returns a warning message when a declared prerequisite cites nothing, and returns nothing for valid records.
sections.why: The comment says this combination should never reach the page, so the warning reports it rather than hiding it.
sections.watch_out: The warning text names the rule that was broken, so keep it aligned with the schema if the rule changes.

sections.name: edgeNoteFor
sections.title: Note on the wave-plan edge
sections.what: Writes a short note saying whether a prerequisite created a wave-plan edge and, if so, which one and why. If none exists, it says the prerequisite produced no edge.
sections.why: The note links a claim on the page to the actual sequencing decision, so a reader can check it.
sections.watch_out: A prerequisite with no matching edge is flagged rather than dropped, so the gap stays visible.

sections.name: costNoteFor
sections.title: Cost note for an unsupported assumption
sections.what: For an unsupported assumption, writes a note explaining the cost in coverage terms. If the future-state confidence block is missing, it says the cost is unknown, not zero.
sections.why: The comment explains that an ungrounded assumption counts as a gap, which reduces coverage and can close the block to zero.
sections.watch_out: The note counts citations minus gaps and clamps at zero, so a block with many gaps can show a cost that is hard to read.

sections.name: ParameterBasis
sections.title: Basis banner for value parameters
sections.what: Shows whether the value parameters are derived from cited figures or are a stated hypothesis. A hypothesis gets a warning saying the process still counts toward the total, with its band widened. A missing confidence block shows a not scored warning.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The comments say the page must not present a hypothesis as if it were a cited figure.
sections.watch_out: The hypothesis test uses both the standing and the score being zero, so a change to either one changes which banner appears.

summary: The process page, which shows one process record at a time. Only its header was reviewed here.
purpose: Shows the scorecard, the bridge, the parameters and the confidence for one process.
why: The header explains the two marks that are shown on the page instead of in a footnote: inverted scores and elapsed time.
how: The header and imports were reviewed. The remaining twenty-four sections, which draw the page and its helpers, were not reviewed, so their steps are unknown here.
inputs: The artifacts, a case id, and the evidence index.
outputs: The process page as drawn HTML.
risks: If a new score runs the other way and is not added to the inverted set, the page will read it backwards and rank the wrong processes.
debug: If a score reads in the wrong direction, check the inverted set at the top of the file. If a figure is missing, check the optional helpers.
